body.statement: At \(d=n\) and \(\sigma=\sigma_n^\star\), carry out \(\mathrm{def:benchmark\text{-}repair\text{-}handle}\): determine the maximal \(\rho_n\) for supportwise feasible, exactly normalized priors with identical design marginals, ATEs concentrated in disjoint intervals separated by \(M\rho_n\), and full-sample total variation at most \(1/3\). Prove either \(\rho_n\sqrt n\to\infty\), which supplies a substantive same-class lower bound inside the accepted parent's residual wedge, or a quantitative obstruction showing that this conditionally centered shared-design program cannot exceed the parametric separation order. Only a benchmark construction that passes exact normalization, realization-wise radius, target concentration, and full-mixture distance may be extended across \(\mathcal W\); no global rate formula is committed before that test.
body.justification: This isolates the first unresolved converse calculation at the benchmark where the accepted parent's rates differ, after the empirical-mass subregion has been removed.
body.gap: Zeng et al. leave intermediate-radius dependence open, and the accepted parent gives only a nonmatching same-class bracket; neither resolves whether a supportwise shared-design marked prior can beat parametric separation at this benchmark.
body.consumer: A passed benchmark identifies whether rare-cell correction can govern risk at \(d=n\); a proved obstruction rules out this converse architecture before a global wedge analysis.
